extra.message: User input from req.body.login is concatenated directly into the SQL string "SELECT name,id FROM Users WHERE login='" + req.body.login + "'" which is executed via db.sequelize.query(query) on line 11 without parameterization. An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL, e.g. a login value of ' OR 1=1-- to dump all users.

User input from req.body.address (POST /app/ping) is concatenated into a shell command passed to child_process.exec('ping -c 2 ' + req.body.address). Because exec() runs the string through a shell, an attacker can inject arbitrary OS commands (e.g. '; cat /etc/passwd') achieving remote code execution.

User input from req.body.eqn (POST /app/calc) is passed directly to mathjs.eval(). mathjs 3.10.1 evaluates expressions with access to the full JavaScript runtime; crafted input can execute arbitrary JavaScript and achieve remote code execution. There is no validation or try/catch around the evaluated expression.

The legacy bulk products endpoint (POST /app/bulkproductslegacy) passes the fully attacker-controlled uploaded file content req.files.products.data.toString('utf8') to node-serialize's serialize.unserialize(). node-serialize 0.0.4 executes serialized functions (e.g. the _$$ND_FUNC$$_ IIFE trick), allowing arbitrary remote code execution via a crafted JSON upload.

The bulk products upload (POST /app/bulkproducts) parses the attacker-supplied XML file with libxmljs.parseXmlString(..., {noent:true, noblanks:true}). The noent:true option enables entity substitution, so an uploaded XML with an external entity declaration such as <!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd"> causes the server to read local files (and could be used for SSRF), with the file contents persisted into product descriptions and displayed back.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: userEditSubmit (POST /app/useredit) looks up the user to modify with db.User.find({ where: { 'id': req.body.id } }) using the user-supplied id without verifying it equals the authenticated user's req.user.id. Any logged-in user can change the email, name and bcrypt-hashed password of any other user (full account takeover) by submitting a different id.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: The admin users API route GET /app/admin/usersapi is protected only by authHandler.isAuthenticated, which checks login state but never checks req.user.role == 'admin'. The /app/admin/users page route (lines 44-46) likewise has no role check; admin functionality is only hidden client-side with JavaScript in views/app/admin.ejs. Any authenticated non-admin user can call the API directly and retrieve all user records.

The password reset token is validated with req.query.token == md5(req.query.login), i.e. the 'secret' token is simply the MD5 hash of the publicly known username (the same flawed check is repeated with req.body.token at line 78). An attacker can compute md5 of any victim's login and reset that user's password via GET/POST /resetpw, achieving complete account takeover of arbitrary accounts.

cwe: CWE-640: Weak Password Recovery Mechanism for Forgotten Password

extra.message: The product search term (req.body.name, set as output.searchTerm in productSearch, core/appHandler.js:68) is rendered with the unescaped EJS tag <%- output.searchTerm %>. An attacker can submit a search query containing <script>...</script> which is reflected unencoded into the HTML response, executing arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's browser.

Product fields rendered with unescaped EJS tags: <%- output.products[i].id %>, <%- ...name %>, <%- ...code %>, <%- ...tags %> and <%- ...description %> (lines 49-53). These values are stored via POST /app/modifyproduct (and the bulk import endpoints) without sanitization, so a product whose name/description contains <script> markup persists malicious HTML that executes in every user's browser viewing the product list (stored XSS).

The admin users page inserts user data from the /app/admin/usersapi JSON response directly via innerHTML: c_id.innerHTML = users[i].id; c_name.innerHTML = users[i].name; c_email.innerHTML = users[i].email; (lines 40-42). User names/emails are attacker-controllable (via registration and POST /app/useredit), so a name like executes as stored DOM-based XSS in the admin's browser when the user list is rendered.

The redirect handler blindly forwards the user to res.redirect(req.query.url) with no validation or allow-listing of the target. The route is registered without any authentication (routes/app.js:48, router.get('/redirect', appHandler.redirect)), so anyone can craft https://host/app/redirect?url=https://evil.com to phish users via an unvalidated redirect from the trusted origin.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: No CSRF protection middleware is ever mounted: the csurf package is declared in package.json but never required in server.js, and none of the state-changing POST routes (/app/modifyproduct, /app/useredit, /app/products, /app/bulkproducts, /app/bulkproductslegacy, /register, /resetpw, /login) issue or validate anti-CSRF tokens. An attacker can forge cross-site requests that add products or change any user's credentials while the victim is logged in.

listUsersAPI executes db.User.findAll({}) with no attribute restriction and returns the raw Sequelize model objects in res.status(200).json({ users: users }). The JSON response therefore includes each user's bcrypt password hash (and any other column) to any authenticated caller, exposing password hashes that can be cracked offline.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: In modifyProductSubmit, the raw error object from the failed product.save() is passed to req.flash('danger', err) and rendered in views/app/modifyproduct.ejs. Sequelize/database errors contain the generated SQL, stack traces and internal file paths, leaking sensitive implementation details to the end user. Similar unhandled errors (e.g. from mathjs.eval at line 197) propagate as stack traces to the client.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: The forgotPw handler responds with 'Invalid login username' when the submitted login does not exist but 'Check email for reset link' when it does (and the resetPw handler at lines 59/64 distinguishes invalid username from invalid token the same way). The differing responses allow an attacker to enumerate valid account logins on the application.

The express-session middleware is initialized with the well-known example secret 'keyboard cat'. Since the secret used to sign session cookies is public knowledge, an attacker can forge a valid signed session cookie and impersonate any user, bypassing authentication.

The session cookie is configured with cookie: { secure: false }, so the session identifier is transmitted over unencrypted HTTP and can be intercepted by a network attacker. The session is also created with saveUninitialized: true, issuing session cookies to unauthenticated visitors.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: The Sequelize instance is constructed without setting logging: false, so Sequelize's default behavior logs every executed SQL statement (including user-supplied values from endpoints such as the injectable userSearch query) to the console via console.log. Sensitive data such as query contents end up in application logs.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: The Express application never disables the X-Powered-By header (no app.disable('x-powered-by') anywhere in server.js), so every response advertises 'X-Powered-By: Express', aiding fingerprinting of the server technology stack. No security headers (Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, etc.) are set either, despite the x-xss-protection package being declared in package.json but never used.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
